title: Suki raises $90M in Series E round to create AI agents
source_used: Healthcare Dive (article body) and Suki's Business Wire release via Yahoo Finance
key_facts: Suki raised $90 million in a Series E round, announced 13 Oct 2026; new investors are Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital, joined by existing investors including Venrock, Flare Capital Partners, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures and Zoom Ventures.
The money will fund AI agents for tasks after a visit such as referrals and prior authorisations of new medications, and deeper work with the more than 30 technology partners that embed Suki's tools.

Suki offers ambient listening and note-taking, automated order entry, billing-code suggestions and patient summaries; athenahealth's Ambient Notes and Zoom's telehealth documentation feature are powered by Suki.
Suki's own release says revenue doubled in 2025 and is on track for similar growth in 2026, and that it serves more than 450 healthcare organisations.
Healthcare Dive: Suki faces heavy competition; Ambience Healthcare raised $243 million and Abridge $300 million last year, while Suki has raised more than $250 million across five rounds.
Founder and CEO Punit Soni: mega rounds of $100 million or more can create unreasonably high expectations; "you should raise only how much you need."
Aman Mahajan of Healthier Capital joins Suki's board.
quote_evidence: As the popularity of AI scribing tools explodes, Suki faces heavy competition in a market where raising hundreds of millions of dollars is not uncommon.

The financing includes new investors Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital, and Hercules Capital, with participation from all existing institutional investors, including Venrock, Flare Capital Partners, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures, and Zoom Ventures.
Revenue doubled in 2025 and is on track for similar growth in 2026, while revenue from its partner business has increased more than tenfold over the past two years.
why_it_matters_hint: A health AI company is moving from note-taking into agents that finish paperwork after a visit, in a crowded and well-funded market.
notes: The Healthcare Dive text lacks the first paragraph (round size context); the Suki press release on Yahoo Finance was used to fill it. Revenue and customer figures are the company's own.
